admission.justification: MIK-R190 rules 6 to 8 put one reader, one atomic file and one judgement across the bridge, the serving tick and the task state, each covered by tests.

applicability: Every limit the product attributes to a role seat, on every send path except the presenter's.
conditions: The host's usage report for that seat is the only source that creates a limit and its reset.

One writer updates provider-limits.json (strictly ar-provider-limits/v1) and its sibling provider-limit-suppressions.json sidecar atomically under provider-limits.lock, and every other reader reads provider-limits.json only; a report holds work solely on an unsuppressed exhausted account-wide window with a future reset.

An enabled extra usage, a positive credits balance, or a window-scoped suppression (auto-tool-call with strict post-limit live turn proof, or operator provider-limits suppress) releases covered windows; a read happens at a new stamped turn end or at the five-minute recheck of a live report.
exclusions: Chat text, error strings and model names produce no limit, and no API key or login store is read.
No usage figure is displayed beyond the limited word and its hover.
An agent with no report, or a full window without a future reset, is not limited.
statement: A limit comes from the host's usage report only: one reader, one locked file pair (provider-limits.json v1 and its sibling provider-limit-suppressions.json sidecar), one projected answer at a time, and no assumption that produces a limit.
title: Host usage report is sole limit creator; suppressions filter live windows
